newsitem.title: USA: Hollywood stars pay tribute to Elizabeth Taylor.
newsitem.headline: Hollywood stars pay tribute to Elizabeth Taylor.

text.p: Hollywood's top stars, including the king of pop and new dad Michael Jackson, turned out Sunday evening to pay tribute to Elizabeth Taylor at a glitzy bash for the film legend's 65th birthday.

Jackson, making his first public appearance since his wife Debbie Rowe Jackson gave birth to their baby boy last Thursday, delivered one of the night's blockbuster tributes to Taylor in a stirring ballad with the refrain "Elizabeth, I love you."
The show stopping performance, however, came from Patti LaBelle, whose soulful compilation of songs brought the house to its feet.

In total, three standing ovations were given during the two hour show, the one for LaBelle and two others for Taylor, who was radiant despite a recent bout with the flu and upcoming surgery to remove a benign brain tumour.
Dressed in an emerald gown and dripping in diamond jewelry, she addressed the audience -- many of whom paid up to $1,000 per ticket for the AIDS charity event -- with a brief statement.

"I'm not here to celebrate my birthday," Taylor said. "I'm here to celebrate all the people in the world with AIDS." She then thanked the audience for their contributions, telling them the money was used for food and services to help combat the disease. The benefit raised more than $1 million.

Taylor arrived at the historic Pantages Theatre in downtown Hollywood escorted by Jackson, who is one of her best friends. He sat beside her through much of the show, appearing exuberant and giving a thumbs up sign to friends in audience.
Singers Rod Stewart and Harry Connick, Jr. rocked the house with music. Actor Hugh Grant and model Elizabeth Hurley gave the event some British flair.

In a smashing black tuxedo, Grant said Taylor was his third favourite Elizabeth, behind Hurley and the Queen of England. Hurley, dressed in a sheer lace gown thanked Taylor for an acting career "jolly, well done."
The queen of pop, Madonna, gave one of the more stirring tributes. Departing from a previously written speech, she praised Taylor for speaking out and fighting against AIDS.
"I adore Elizabeth Taylor and the movies. But it is the work she has done in the past 12 years that makes her a star," Madonna said. "You are the most golden of stars. Happy Birthday."
The violet-eyed Taylor debuted on the silver screen at the age of 10 in 1942's "Lassie Come Home". She skyrocketed to fame just two years later as the horse loving little girl in "National Velvet."

Her film career peaked in the late 1950's and 1960's in films like "Cat on a Hot Tin Roof", "Butterfield 8" and "Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf." Her work in the latter two both earned Taylor Academy Awards.

Though her storybook rise in the movies has been fodder for newspapers and books, it is Taylor's personal life that has caused the most scandalous headlines in tabloids and on television talk shows around the globe.

At age 17, she was engaged for the first time to All American football hero, Glenn Davis, but the two soon broke up. Four years later she married Conrad "Nicky" Hilton. It was the first of eight nuptial episodes for Taylor.
She wed actor Richard Burton twice -- both torrid affairs that ended in divorce.
In the 70's and '80's, Taylor battled weight problems and alcohol and drug dependency, but eventually exorcised those demons.
